Friday, March 15, 2019 
 
 
 
103 
 
 
LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY OF MANITOBA 
__________________________ 
 
VOTES AND PROCEEDINGS   No. 26 
 
FOURTH SESSION, FORTY-FIRST LEGISLATURE 
 
PRAYER 10:00 O'CLOCK A.M. 
 
Immediately following the Prayer, Mr. LINDSEY rose on a Matter of Privilege regarding comments 
made by the Premier in the House on March 14, 2019 related to the Mining Community Reserve fund , 
contending that the Premier had knowingly misled the House and moved: 
 
THAT the matter of the Premier knowingly misleading Manitobans about the Government’s 
inaction in the face of a jobs crisis in the North be moved to an all-party committee immediately. 
 
And Hon. Messrs. GOERTZEN and GERRARD having spoken. 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Subsequently following the Prayer, Mr. WIEBE rose on a Matter of Privilege regarding comments 
made by the Premier indicating an intention to ignore the provisions in the Elections Act regarding the fixed 
election date and moved: 
 
THAT this matter be referred to an all-party committee immediately. 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Subsequently following the Prayer , Mrs. SMITH (Point Douglas) rose on a Matter of Privilege 
regarding proposed changes to election rebates and moved: 
 
THAT this matter be referred to an all-party committee immediately. 
 
And Hon. Mr. GOERTZEN having spoken. 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Subsequently following the Prayer,  Ms. LATHLIN rose on a Matter of Privilege regarding the 
government’s intention to introduce Conflict of Interest legislation and misleading statements made by the 
Premier regarding his involvement with a private company and moved: 
 
THAT this matter, especially the Costa Rica part,  be moved to an all -party committee for 
consideration. 

=====PAGE
Friday, March 15, 2019 
 
 
 
104 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Subsequently following the Prayer, Mr. WIEBE rose on a Matter of Privilege regarding a 
statement made in the House on March 14, 2019 by Hon. Mr. GOERTZEN and requested that the Minister 
of Education and Training apologize to the Superintendent of the Winnipeg School Division and moved: 
 
THAT the Minister of Education ’s statements, which are an attack on the administration of 
Manitoba School Boards, be moved to an all-party committee immediately. 
 
And Hon. Mr. GOERTZEN having spoken. 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Subsequently following the Prayer Mr. WIEBE rose on a Matter of Privilege regarding a letter sent 
to the Speaker of the House by the Leader of the Official Opposition in 2017 relating to the need for the 
Assembly to include a treaty land acknowledgement in the operations of the House and moved: 
 
THAT the issue of treaty land acknowledgement be immediately referred to the Rules Committee 
for consideration and that the committee report back to the House at the earliest opportunity. 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Subsequently following the Prayer Mr. LINDSEY rose on a Matter of Privilege regarding the 
Government Caucus spreading false information about NDP Members and moved: 
 
THAT this issue be immediately referred to a committee of this House. 
 
WHEREUPON Madam Speaker informed the House she would take the matter under advisement. 
______________________________ 
 
Hon. Mr. FIELDING moved and outlined its purposes: 
 
THAT Bill (No. 21) – The Legislative Building Centennial Restoration and Preservation Act, be 
now read a First Time. 
 
And the Question being put.  It was agreed to, on the following division:

The House then adjourned at 12:31 p.m. until 1:30 p.m. Monday, March 18, 2019.
